statement: A pattern goes 2, 5, 8, 11, ... What number comes next?

choices.misconception: I added 1, as if the numbers just count up one at a time.
I counted on 3 from 11 but said 11 as my first count, so I said 11, 12, 13.
I skipped a number and gave the one after next: 14 and then 17.
I doubled 11 instead of looking at how much each number grows.

hints: How far is it from each number to the next?
Find the jump between neighbours in the pattern. Check that the jump is the same every time, then make that same jump once more from the last number.
From 2 to 5, from 5 to 8 and from 8 to 11 the jump is 3 each time. Count on 3 from 11.

solutions.reliable: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 2, 5, 8, 11. Counting on 3 from 11 gives 12, 13, 14, so the next number is 14. The idea to keep: find the jump between neighbours, check it is always the same, then use it once more.

whyOnTest: Continuing a pattern tests whether a child finds the rule from every step, not just guesses from the last number.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
